narratives.title: Typical vs slammed
narratives.summary: Compared with Typical, Slammed shows higher synthetic task pressure (+369 tasks) and more deferred synthetic work (+320 tasks). The queue-depth signal is larger (+11) while approximate walking load also rises (+10204 feet). This is an operational comparison only using synthetic, seeded scenario output.
limitations: Synthetic tasks use explicit assumptions and seeded generation.
nonClaims: Not based on real patient, staff, EHR, or hospital data.

narratives.title: Typical vs walking heavy
narratives.summary: Compared with Typical, Walking heavy shows higher approximate walking load (+29428 feet). It also carries higher synthetic task pressure (+216 tasks), more deferred synthetic work (+186 tasks), and a larger queue-depth signal (+9). This narrative is an operational comparison only, not a staffing or clinical recommendation.
limitations: Synthetic tasks use explicit assumptions and seeded generation.
nonClaims: Not based on real patient, staff, EHR, or hospital data.

narratives.title: Typical vs trauma heavy
narratives.summary: Compared with Typical, Trauma heavy produces higher synthetic task pressure (+112 tasks) with a trauma workload notice in the warning signal set. The same comparison shows more deferred synthetic work (+77 tasks), higher approximate walking load (+7100 feet), and a larger queue-depth signal (+4). This is an operational comparison only and stays limited to deterministic Plan 1 demo evidence.
limitations: Synthetic tasks use explicit assumptions and seeded generation.
nonClaims: Not based on real patient, staff, EHR, or hospital data.

narratives.title: Overall demo summary
narratives.summary: The Plan 1 comparison set separates synthetic workload patterns into task pressure, deferred synthetic work, approximate walking load, and queue-depth signals. Slammed is the strongest task-pressure contrast, Walking heavy is the clearest walking-load contrast, and Trauma heavy adds the trauma workload notice without changing the proof into a recommendation. All summaries are operational comparison only and use deterministic synthetic evidence.
limitations: Synthetic tasks use explicit assumptions and seeded generation.
nonClaims: Not based on real patient, staff, EHR, or hospital data.
